title: Indirect prompt injection
model: Bing Chat; GPT-4 synthetic applications; code-completion engines
system: LLM-integrated applications processing retrieved external content
organization: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security; Saarland University; sequire technology

cells.title: Source
body: Kai Greshake, Sahar Abdelnabi, Shailesh Mishra, Christoph Endres, Thorsten Holz, and Mario Fritz submitted "Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection" to arXiv on February 23, 2023.
The paper studied attacks in which an adversary places instructions in data likely to be retrieved by an LLM-integrated application.

cells.title: Observed behavior
body: The paper reported that instructions embedded in retrieved content could alter the behavior of LLM-integrated applications even though the user had not directly issued those instructions.
The authors demonstrated attacks against real-world systems, including Bing Chat and code-completion engines, and against synthetic GPT-4 applications.

cells.output: The paper described adversaries remotely exploiting LLM-integrated applications by injecting prompts into data likely to be retrieved at inference time.
The authors argued that LLM-integrated applications blur the line between data and instructions.

cells.title: Provenance
body: Primary source: arXiv:2302.12173, submitted February 23, 2023 and last revised May 5, 2023.
The case uses the arXiv abstract and paper metadata for the artifact description. Specific exploit transcripts should be added only from the paper if they are excerpted precisely.

cells.title: Notes
body: This file records the paper as the primary artifact. It does not reproduce exploit payloads from the paper in detail.
